Enflasyon: The tendency of the general price level to rise continuously. Inflation is measured by the official indices published by TUIK (Turkish Statistical Institute) that track consumer and producer price developments.
Faiz oranı: The ratio of the interest to be paid to the borrowed amount.
Likidite: A measure of how easily an asset or security traded in the market can be bought or sold without affecting its market price. Assets or securities with high liquidity are also expected to have high trading volumes.
Ayı Piyasası: Refers to markets in which prices are falling.
Boğa Piyasası: Refers to a market in which prices are rising.
Birincil Piyasa: The market where first-time issuances take place. The first launch (sale) of an investment instrument, for example a security, is a primary market transaction. Likewise, the auction-based sale of government domestic debt securities by the Ministry of Treasury and Finance of the Republic of Türkiye is also a primary market transaction. Subsequent purchases and sales of these securities among investors take place in markets known as the secondary market.
Brüt kâr marjı: The ratio of gross profit (sales minus cost of goods sold) to sales; it measures cost-of-production discipline.
Cari işlemler hesabı: The main item in the balance of payments showing trade and income flows.
Dezenflasyon: Means a slowdown in the pace of price increases. It refers to the disinflation process experienced during the transition from high inflation to lower inflation.
Finansal kaldıraç: The effect of debt financing on magnifying return on equity; it cuts both ways, since it also enlarges losses in low-profit periods.
Kaldıraç: Enlarging a position using debt or derivatives; it magnifies both returns and losses by the same proportion.
Fiyat-kazanç oranı: The ratio of the share price to earnings per share; it shows the price an investor pays for 1 lira of earnings and should be compared across sectors.
Beta katsayısı: The sensitivity of an asset's return to the market return; β=1 means moving with the market, β>1 means volatility above the market.
Basit Faiz Oranı: The interest rate at which an investment earns interest only on its principal during the investment period.
Bileşik Faiz Oranı: The interest reflecting the return obtained when the interest earned by an investment over the investment period is reinvested along with the principal. In other words, interest earning interest.
Gayri safi yurtiçi hasıla: Or in short GDP, the market value of all final goods and services produced using a country's resources in a given period.
Açık enflasyon hedeflemesi: A monetary policy regime in which the central bank determines, under explicit rules, how it will use monetary policy instruments to achieve its inflation target.
Zorunlu Karşılık Oranı: The statutory ratio showing the amount of reserves that banks and other financial institutions are required to hold at the central bank against the deposits, loans and similar liabilities on their balance sheets. The reserve requirement ratio may differ according to the type, maturity and currency of the liabilities. Central banks can use this ratio as a monetary policy instrument. If banks do not hold idle reserves, an increase in the reserve requirement ratio leads banks to call back the loans they have extended, which causes the money supply to contract. When the ratio is lowered, part of the required reserves turns into usable reserves, which increases the banks' lending base; the expansion of the banks' lending base in turn causes the money supply to grow.
Temettü verimi: The ratio of annual dividends per share to the share price; it shows the investor's cash return.
Temettü dağıtım oranı: Shows what portion of net profit is distributed as dividends (Dividends / Net profit); the remainder is reinvested as internal funding.
Tarihsel volatilite: The standard deviation calculated from the past return series; unlike implied volatility, it is based on history rather than expectations.
Reel faiz: Interest stripped of inflation; by the Fisher equation (1+real) = (1+nominal)/(1+inflation), approximately real ≈ nominal − inflation.
Piyasa değeri: The price of goods and services jointly determined by supply and demand in a free market.
Tahvil: Securities with a maturity of one year or more, for which the issuing institution promises a specified repayment at maturity.
Serbest nakit akışı: The portion of cash generated from operating activities that remains after capital expenditures are deducted; it is an input to DCF valuation.
Vadeli işlem: A standardized exchange-traded contract containing the obligation to buy or sell a specific asset at a specific price on a specific date; daily settlement (mark-to-market) applies.
Nominal faiz oranı: Or in short i, the percentage borrowers pay to lenders without adjusting for price changes caused by inflation.
Tüketici Fiyat Endeksi -TÜFE: An index measuring changes in the prices of goods and services purchased by consumers. In calculating the CPI, first the expenditures made over a year on goods and services by a sample population representing the country as a whole are compiled. According to this expenditure structure, the relative weights of goods and services within the index are determined; goods and services consumed in large amounts by the sample population carry higher weights, while less-consumed ones carry lower weights. The prices of the determined goods and services are collected from all provinces on specific days of each month. The CPI is calculated using the collected prices and the weights set at the start of the year.
Marj çağrısı: A demand by the brokerage for additional collateral when the collateral in a leveraged position falls below the required level; if it is not met, the position is liquidated.
Kur Riski: Refers to the possibility of incurring losses due to changes in assets and/or liabilities resulting from fluctuations in the future exchange rate. Methods to hedge against exchange rate risk include investors taking positions in both financial and goods markets, investing in the financial markets of multiple countries, and using derivative products or markets.
Analitik Bilanço/TCMB Analitik Bilançosu: An analytical balance sheet is one in which the accounts on the asset and liability sides are netted against one another and consolidated under appropriate groupings. The CBRT Analytical Balance Sheet consolidates the items on the CBRT balance sheet taking into account the items relevant to the effective conduct of monetary policy, without detailed breakdowns. In line with the functioning of monetary policy, 'Foreign Assets', 'Domestic Assets' and 'Valuation Account' appear under 'Assets', while 'Total Foreign Currency Liabilities' and 'Central Bank Money' appear under 'Liabilities'. For the CBRT Analytical Balance Sheet
Bankalararası faiz oranı: Or in short IBOR, the interest rate banks pay one another for uncollateralized daily borrowing in the money market.
Gini katsayısı: Or in short G, a statistical measure showing to what extent a group of numbers differs from one another, generally used to calculate inequality.
Hiperenflasyon: Although there is no precise definition, the situation in which the monthly inflation rate is 50 percent or higher.
Kayıtdışı ekonomi: Business and production activities taking place in a country without the knowledge and supervision of the state.
Kaldıraç Oranı: The ratio of debt to equity or to total capital. Leverage ratios show a business's funding structure and make it possible to see what resources finance its assets and in what proportion. The leverage ratio developed under Basel III is calculated by dividing core capital by the total risk amount.
Likidite Riski: Refers to funding and market liquidity risk. Funding risk is the risk of an additional funding need arising from a mismatch between short-term cash inflows and outflows, while market liquidity risk refers to the risk involving the time and value at which financial assets can be converted into cash.
Likidite tuzağı: The situation in which increasing the money supply fails to affect aggregate demand because the nominal interest rate has fallen to its lowest possible level.
Maliyet itişli enflasyon: Inflation that arises as a result of increases in production factor or raw material prices across the economy.
Net kâr marjı: The ratio of net profit to sales (Net profit / Sales) and the first component of the DuPont analysis; it shows how much net profit remains from every 1 lira of sales.
Politika faiz oranı: The interest rate that the central bank sets and effectively manages in line with its policy objectives.
Reel Faiz Oranı: The nominal interest rate stripped of inflation. Technically, it is found by subtracting the expected inflation rate from the nominal interest rate.
Talep çekişli enflasyon: Inflation that arises as a result of an increase in aggregate product demand across the economy.
Tamamlayıcı mal: Products that are used together to a certain extent.
Tüketici fiyat endeksi: Or in short CPI, a price index based on goods and services oriented toward the consumption of the average household as the product basket.
Vadeli mevduat: Bank accounts that provide a monetary return in exchange for not using the money for a predetermined period.
Vadeli Piyasalar: Forward markets are markets in which contracts are bought and sold that contain the commitment to deliver a specific product at a future date, on the condition that its price is fixed today.
Vadeye Dayalı Zorunlu Karşılıklar: The required reserve amount that banks and other financial institutions must hold at the CBRT against their liabilities varies according to the maturity of those liabilities. Reserve requirement ratios are higher for short-term liabilities and lower for long-term ones. Thereby, by encouraging longer-term liabilities, the aim is to extend the average maturity of banks' liabilities.
Zımni volatilite: The volatility backed out from the option's market price; it is the market's measurable expectation of future volatility.
Çekirdek Enflasyon: The permanent component of inflation stripped of temporary or one-off effects. Excluding certain items from the index, statistical analysis and model-based methods are frequently used in calculating core inflation; however, the most widely followed core inflation indicators are those obtained by the exclusion method. For this purpose, energy prices, basic food prices and indirect taxes, which are more exposed to external effects (energy prices, seasonal conditions, fiscal policy, etc.) and can be temporary in nature, are the main elements excluded from such inflation calculations. The purpose of using core inflation is to identify the elements that make the change in the general price level persistent. Although the inflation target is set on headline CPI inflation, the course of core inflation indicators is also taken into account so that more realistic policy decisions can be taken. In particular, in countries moving toward inflation targeting, rather than a single core inflation indicator, alternative indices calculated in different ways are followed, considering the advantages and disadvantages of all calculation methods.
Belirsizlik: The state of not knowing exactly how a future event will turn out.
Denge faiz oranı: The interest rate at which borrowing and lending transactions take place when the money market is in equilibrium.
Enflasyon Beklentileri: Refers to the projections of economic units regarding inflation that has not yet materialized (will occur in the future). To measure inflation expectations, indices derived from various market instruments or surveys such as the Survey of Expectations published by the CBRT can be used.
Enflasyon Risk Primi: Refers to the risk premium added to the real interest rate to compensate for the loss that would occur if inflation materialized above the expected level. In other words, the nominal interest rate contains the real interest rate, inflation expectations and the inflation risk premium. This risk premium arises in countries where inflation fluctuations and uncertainties are present.
Marjinal fayda: Or in short MU, the additional utility gained from consuming one more unit of a product in a given period.
Gösterge faiz oranı: The minimum interest rate investors will demand for a non-government security.
Özel kesim tahvili oranı: The interest rate on securities issued by private banks and corporations into the market.
Marjinal tüketim eğilimi: Or in short MPC, the change observed in private consumption expenditures when total income in an economy increases by one unit.
Son çare borç sağlayıcı: The institution that is willing to lend even when no one else is.
